citation: Primary: Martian (Zverianskii, Zhang, Clyne, Garcia, Barez, Upadhyay), Code Review Bench, https://codereview.withmartian.com/ and https://github.com/withmartian/code-review-benchmark (MIT, launched Feb 2026 as v0). Academic: (1) Lin, Liang, Thongtanunam, Tantithamthavorn, 'Is Agentic Code Review Helpful? Mining Developers' Feedback to CodeRabbit Reviews in the Wild', arXiv:2607.03316, Jul 2026 (v2 23 Jul). (2) Cynthia, Widyasari, Roy, Zhang, Lo, 'Go Home Copilot, You're Drunk', arXiv:2607.21997, Jul 2026. (3) Chowdhury, Banik, Ferdous, Shamim, 'From Industry Claims to Empirical Reality: An Empirical Study of Code Review Agents in Pull Requests', MSR 2026, arXiv:2604.03196. (4) Cihan et al., 'Automated Code Review In Practice', ICSE 2025 SEIP, arXiv:2412.18531. (5) Kumar, Bararia, Raj, 'Bigger Isn't Always Better', arXiv:2606.15689 (Apr 2026).
source_tier: Martian benchmark: independent-of-vendors open-source benchmark run by a third party, not peer reviewed. Academic: MSR 2026 (peer reviewed), ICSE 2025 SEIP (peer reviewed), three arXiv preprints (2607.03316, 2607.21997, 2606.15689) with no venue named on the page.
access_status: Martian GitHub README: fully read via fetch. Martian leaderboard site codereview.withmartian.com: opened but page returned only a title (JavaScript app), so live numbers NOT read directly [uncertain]; leaderboard numbers come from third-party article aicodereviews.io (read) and vendor blogs (search snippets only). arXiv papers: abstract pages read via fetch (summarised by fetch tool, not full text); no full PDFs read. Quriosity-agent GitHub write-up of Feb 2026 snapshot read.
sponsor_and_incentive: Martian: README names no funding and no commercial tie to ranked tools [uncertain whether Martian sells a competing code review product; README does not say]. Martian itself runs the pipeline for published tools. Vendors (CodeRabbit, Greptile, Cubic) publish their own '#1 on Martian' posts, so figures quoted in vendor posts carry marketing incentive. Academic papers: none of the five arXiv/conference pages state funding [uncertain]. Cihan et al. studied a tool built on open-source Qodo PR Agent in an industrial deployment (authors' employer not confirmed on page [uncertain]). None of the academic studies were run by the tool vendors as far as the pages show. Chowdhury et al. and Lin et al. use public repository data; Lin et al. examine CodeRabbit only.
exact_quotes: Martian README: "50 PRs from 5 major open-source projects, each with human-verified golden comments." (offline track; 173 golden comments)
Martian README: "Static datasets risk training data leakage" (reason given for the online track)

aicodereviews.io (third-party, 5 Oct 2026 board): "The online benchmark continuously samples fresh PRs where review bots already left comments."

arXiv 2607.03316 abstract (paraphrase by fetch tool, not verbatim): reviews receive 'mixed reception'; rejections mainly tied to invalid suggestions such as false positives, redundant, or out of scope.
key_claims: Martian Code Review Bench: two tracks. Offline = 50 PRs (Sentry, Grafana, Cal.com, Discourse, Keycloak) with 173 human golden comments, LLM judge (Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-5.2, Sonnet 4.5). Online = fresh public PRs where bots commented; a three-step LLM pipeline extracts bot suggestions, extracts human fixes, matches them. Online precision = share of bot suggestions that matched a real post-review fix; recall = share of developer fixes the bot had flagged. It does NOT report a false positive rate. Academic: Lin et al. find agentic CodeRabbit reviews mostly rejected (56.3%). Chowdhury et al. find CRA-only PRs merge less than human-only PRs and most closed CRA-only PRs are low signal. Cynthia et al. find inline code suggestions the strongest predictor of comment resolution, and incorrect suggestions and intentional design decisions the main reasons comments go unresolved. Cihan et al. find 73.8% of automated comments resolved but PR closure time rose. Kumar et al. find real-PR F1 collapses versus synthetic bugs.
headline_figures: LEAD CHECK: 'Martian Bench shows top AI review agents with 40 to 70% false positive rates' is NOT supported. Martian reports precision/recall/F1, not false positive rate. Among top-5 tools precision is about 67-80% on the Oct 2026 board (implied non-matching share of roughly 20-33% if you treat 1-precision as false positives, an inference, not a Martian claim). Feb 2026 snapshot (Quriosity write-up of launch, last two months): CodeRabbit F1 51.3%, precision 49.2%, recall 53.5%; Cursor precision 67.9%, recall 36.4%; Copilot F1 43.5%; ChatGPT Codex F1 39.8%. Implied non-adoption 32% to 52% for those tools, which only loosely resembles 40-70% and only for early snapshot and only as 1-precision. 5 Oct 2026 board (aicodereviews.io, last-month view): Cubic Dev AI F1 65.5 / P 72.4 / R 59.8 (n=1,551); Greptile 62.3 / 80.5 / 50.8 (n=1,564); GitHub Copilot 61.5 / 66.8 / 57.0 (n=925); Claude 61.3 / 69.0 / 55.2 (n=995); CodeRabbit 61.0 / 68.6 / 55.0 (n=2,084); CodeAnt AI 48.9 F1 rank 14; spread across 14 tools about 17 F1 points. Vendor claims: CodeRabbit Mar 2026 51.2% F1; Greptile Jul 2026 60.8% F1, 76.2% P, 50.6% R; Cubic 65.7% F1, 73.2% P, 59.6% R (vendor blog, snippet only [uncertain]). Note 'precision' online is adoption-based proxy, so unaddressed-but-valid comments count as misses. Academic: Lin et al. (n=31,073 review/feedback pairs, 10,191 PRs, 239 repos, CodeRabbit only): 36.4% accepted, 7.3% discussion, 56.3% rejected; lightweight models predict rejection up to 76% F1. Cynthia et al.: 54,791 comments (snippet said 54,713), five agents (Copilot, Cursor, Codex, Devin, Claude), 342 Python repos; Copilot 72.9% of resolved comments (abstract wording is 'accounted for'; not a per-agent resolution rate, snippet misread it as such). Chowdhury et al. (AIDev dataset, 19,450 PRs, 3,109 analysed): CRA-only merge rate 45.20% vs human-only 68.37% (23.17 pt gap); of 98 closed CRA-only PRs, 60.2% in 0-30% signal range; 12 of 13 CRAs below 60% average signal ratio. Cihan et al.: 73.8% of automated comments resolved; 1,568 PRs with automated reviews of 4,335; mean closure time 5h52m to 8h20m; 238 practitioners, 10 projects. Kumar et al.: best model real-PR F1 0.066 vs 0.847 synthetic; Haiku 4.5 F1 0.365 vs Sonnet 4.6 0.343; F1 0.657 on diffs under 10 lines vs 0.043 over 150 lines. Related but separate: GitHub ReviewBench (GitHub blog, tops at 40.1% grounded F1 for Copilot; GitHub is a vendor, snippet only [uncertain]).
sample_and_method: Martian: observational, LLM-judged matching of bot comments to later human fixes (online) and to golden comments (offline). Maintainers run the pipeline themselves. Tool must be attributable (bot account or marker). Lin et al.: mined GitHub review/feedback pairs, manual and LLM classification. Cynthia et al.: mined Python repos, open card sort of 470 unresolved discussions. Chowdhury et al.: AIDev dataset comparison of CRA-only vs human-only PRs. Cihan et al.: industrial case study with PR data and surveys (22-person broader survey). Kumar et al.: 150 samples, 100 synthetic mutations plus 50 real bug-fix PRs, five LLMs (not commercial review products).
limitations: Martian: precision is an adoption proxy; LLM judge; offline set only 50 PRs and possible training leakage (README says so); leaderboard excludes private repos and tools with few public PRs; rankings move daily and vendor '#1' claims go stale within months; Martian funding and any commercial interest undisclosed on pages I read; I could not read the live leaderboard. Academic: Lin et al. single tool; Cynthia et al. Python only, five agents, correlational; Chowdhury et al. merge rate confounded by PR type and who opens PRs; Cihan et al. one company, three projects analysed, closure time confounded; Kumar et al. tests raw LLMs not products. 'Rejected' or 'unresolved' does not prove a comment was wrong. Several figures come from fetch-tool summaries of abstract pages, not full-text reading.
what_a_leader_can_do: Do not buy on a vendor's '#1 on Martian' claim; ask for the date, sample size and precision/recall split. Measure your own acceptance rate of AI comments per tool (the studies show 36-74% depending on tool and setting). Require concrete inline suggestions, which Cynthia et al. link to resolution. Keep humans in the loop: CRA-only PRs merged less often. Evidence strength: moderate for acceptance-rate measurement (several observational studies); weak for any causal effect on quality.
overlap_with_site_essays: Strong overlap with What It Takes to Trust Agent Output (need independent, dated measurement rather than vendor claims) and Checking Isn't Catching (accepted or resolved comments are not the same as caught defects; Martian precision is an adoption proxy). Some overlap with The Verification Gap (low-signal comments add checking load, closure time rose in Cihan et al.). Little direct overlap with Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part, beyond noise adding reviewer load.
